bearings.paper_claim: Paper says greedy path extraction after map changes can deadlock where a predecessor cost value exceeds its successor value (Fig. 3b). Its fix (Eq. 6, Algorithm 2) picks the unexplored successor minimizing passage cost plus g and excludes explored nodes. The 18,468 vs 28,351 freezing node counts compare the whole improved method (local update plus extraction plus path optimization) with the original D* Lite, not Eq. 6 alone. The paper does not say the g values are out of date or made consistent with the change.
bearings.paper_location: Sec. 2.3, Eq. 6, Algorithm 2, Fig. 3, pp. 6-8; Table 3, p. 15
bearings.system_side: Dashboard buildPath runs one max-product Dijkstra from the target (distToTarget). distToTarget does not check the dropped set, while tracePath skips dropped members. When members are dropped, dT still counts routes through them, so the greedy trace can be suboptimal or return reached=false. The code comment labels the chain PROVABLY-OPTIMAL. With nothing dropped the extraction is exact.

bearings.transfer_conditions: The mechanism is general graph search and does not depend on ice data, so it applies to the 533-node cosponsor graph whenever the member-out scenario is active. The paper's timings (single voyage, no hardware stated) do not transfer. Fix is a full recompute that honors dropped, which is cheap at this size.
bearings.verifier_note: Code read and confirmed (line numbers match). Not run, so UNVERIFIED under DE-062 until the dashboard is run with a dropped member and compared with a Dijkstra that honors dropped. Paper side softened as stated in paper_claim. The directed-symmetry question (PE assumed symmetric) is unchecked.

bearings.paper_claim: Paper's local-update rule (Eq. 5) cuts node updates by 34.9% (freezing) and 79.5% (melting) against the original D* Lite and planning time by 46.2% and 85.7%. Route length differs from full re-planning by about 0.1% (2,558.747 vs 2,561.408 n mi freezing; 2,419.087 vs 2,418.146 n mi melting). The paper gives no optimality guarantee; it reports error below 0.1% against the global re-planning routes.
bearings.paper_location: Sec. 2.2, Eq. 5, Algorithm 1; Sec. 4.1-4.2; Tables 3-4, pp. 15-17
bearings.system_side: Staffer router is an exact bidirectional Dijkstra with heuristic 0. Ties are costs within 1e-12 relative, broken by fewer steps. Results are cached under a key that includes the graph revision, so a revision change forces a fresh search. No incremental reuse exists.
bearings.code_ref: fec/surfaces/staffer_closeness_routes.py:1-21 (exact search and tie docstring); :79 (ALGORITHM string); fec/surfaces/staffer_routing.py:386 (heuristic 0); :567-572 (revision-keyed cache)
bearings.transfer_conditions: Incremental replanning helps when the same origin and goal are re-queried after small local edge changes on a large graph. Staffer requests use different origins and targets, so the paper's gains do not transfer directly. The approximate update would conflict with an exact-cost requirement.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper numbers match Tables 3-4 (34.9, 79.5, 46.2, 85.7 percent; distance gaps 0.10 percent freezing and 0.04 percent melting). Code side confirmed (heuristic 0, bidirectional Dijkstra, 1e-12 tie width, revision-keyed cache). Not verified from inputs: the 4.66M overlap-pair count, the 2026-10-02 ALT deferral, and the 2026-10-03 exact-tie ruling.

bearings.paper_claim: Paper reports node updates of 18,468 vs 72,835 (freezing) and 16,864 vs 114,929 (melting) for its improved D* Lite against full global re-planning. Numbers are correct. The paper frames reuse of earlier search data as the motivation (Sec. 2.1) but does not say D* Lite family planners save work only by reuse.
bearings.system_side: scenario.py docstring (line 13) cites Ren et al. Multi-Objective Path-Based D* Lite for recompute only what the scenario touches. The code uses common random numbers (cascade, around :42-52) and recomputes spread and flip value for every category (:103-115). Isolation comes from CRN, not from reusing earlier search state.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Documentation point only. At 533 members and MC=40 a full recompute is cheap, so incremental reuse is not warranted. The Xu numbers say nothing about the cascade. The cited work is Ren et al., not Xu.
bearings.verifier_note: Numbers and line references confirmed. Softened because the only claim is absent from Xu and the docstring cites Ren, not Xu. The bearing supports a docstring correction only, not a result about the paper.

bearings.paper_claim: Paper uses cost = delta*r + d (Eq. 12). Raising delta from 1 to 3 at Icemax 1.2 m (freezing) lowers average risk from 0.076 to 0.039 and lengthens the route from 2,558.7 to 2,645.5 n mi (+3.4%) (Table 5). Paper calls delta = 3 sufficient based on simulation experiments it does not show. The text does not call them unpublished. The paper shows no Pareto front.
bearings.system_side: cosponsor_route.py builds greedy routes with a lambda risk penalty (value = (gain - lambda(1-p))/cost) over lambda in {0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4}, then keeps non-dominated (cost, spread, risk) points. It is not a shortest-path search. The file header cites MOPBD* (conceptual).
bearings.code_ref: fec/engine/cosponsor_route.py:40-63 (greedy lambda route); :64-76 (non-dominated filter over lambda sweep); file header (MOPBD* citation)
bearings.transfer_conditions: The two works share only the weighted-sum risk cost. The system reports a front while the paper fixes one delta. Weighted-sum scalarization can miss non-convex front points in both.
bearings.verifier_note: Table 5 numbers confirmed. Softened for the unpublished wording, which is not in the paper. A text search found no Pareto front in the paper.

related.why: Verified: Multi-Objective Path-Based D* Lite (IEEE RA-L 2022). Its use in scenario.py and cosponsor_route.py is at docstring level only.

Verified: improved D* Lite for forest-firefighting UAVs. Its changes are map zooming and spline smoothing, not local replanning, so the parallel to Xu is only that both modify D* Lite for a specific domain.
Verified: D* Lite as the low-level planner inside CBS for multi-agent dynamic replanning. Shares the incremental-replanning base, with a multi-agent setting.
Verified: most reliable path maximizes on-time arrival probability. The dashboard comment at make_dashboard_html_00.tpl:735-739 cites it for the max-product chain.
Verified: from-scratch directed single-source shortest paths. It is the opposite strategy to Xu's reuse of earlier search state.

summary_issues: summary_md says the paper shows scenario.py's D* Lite citation overclaims reuse. The paper never mentions scenario.py. That is a Melange-side finding, not a paper finding.

paul_alignment says Paul marked D* replanning Very interesting and that his addendum made D* Lite the operational layer. Neither is in the inputs (paul_entries and paul_markup are empty). Unverified; remove or source it.
Related link lawande-2022 is wrong. That paper compares Dijkstra, A*, BFS and Greedy Best First on video-game grids; it is not a D*-family survey. Dropped.
Related link luo-2020 why-text said its local-replanning changes parallel Xu's. Its changes are map zooming and spline smoothing. Corrected in related.
Bearing 4 says unpublished simulations. The paper says only that simulation experiments showed delta 3 near-peak (Sec. 3.2, p. 12). Corrected.

The paper's 0.07 percent error figures do not reproduce. Tables 3-4 give distance gaps of 0.10 percent (freezing, same for original and global) and 0.04 percent (melting). Quote the table-derived values only.
Paper says 8 grid units is about 432 n mi. At 25 km per cell 8 units is about 200 km, or about 108 n mi. Internal inconsistency in the paper; not resolved.
Paper timing reductions round differently from its tables: 924 vs 1,720 s is 46.3 percent and 924 vs 3,392 s is 72.8 percent; the text says 46.2 and 72.7. Rounding only.
Paper's conclusion says planning efficiency rose 35 percent, but 34.9 is the node-update reduction and 46.2 the planning-time reduction. Do not repeat it as an efficiency figure.
Paper text says risk rises with Icemax (Sec. 4.3), but its own Table 5 melting sweep at delta 1 gives 0.625, 0.631, 0.615. Rel flags this correctly.
Paper's proportionality claim (gains proportional to ice-data completeness) rests on two periods. Rel flags it as untested, which is correct.
Not verifiable from inputs: the 2026-10-02 ALT deferral, the 2026-10-03 exact-tie ruling as Paul's rule, and the 4.66M overlap-pair count (not found in staffer_routing.py). Treat as unverified.
Repo search for D* Lite or LPA* implementations in fec/ found none. Output was capped at 40 lines, but no D* implementation names appeared. The no-incremental-replanning claim holds on this evidence.
Dashboard finding (distToTarget ignores dropped) is code-confirmed but not run. UNVERIFIED under DE-062 until reproduced.
Paper has no hardware specification and reports one voyage per period with no variance. Rel's limitation list is correct on both points.
